warming 3.26 °C, σ 2.35 °C → S/N 1.39; 47% of recent years warmer than any 1850–1900 one
warming 3.58 °C, σ 1.61 °C → S/N 2.22; 73% of recent years warmer than any 1850–1900 one

svg.text: Signal-to-noise is what makes a change visible. Winter warmed as much as summer, but a single winter swings by ±2.3 °C (σ), so most recent winters still fall inside the 1850–1900
range: the red and grey ticks overlap. Summer nights vary by only ±0.9 °C, so a 3.1 °C warming carries them clear of the old climate: 28 of the last 30 summers were warmer than
the warmest pre-industrial one (dashed line), against 14 of 30 winters. Climate scientists call the moment a season's signal leaves its noise its time of emergence; it comes first
where the noise is small (summer, the tropics), not where the warming is largest. Hover a tick for its year.
